messages:
ryan: Heads-up — saw a reproducible latency spike on canary when sequence lengths jump from 8->64. nsys trace shows repeated Triton/JIT compile events (~35–45ms each) interleaved with kernel launches, total token latency +120ms.

maria: link to perfetto/nvsys?

ryan: https://perf.company/redwood/trace/1842501123 (nsys export attached). nvtx shows `kernel_select` -> `triton:compile` tags.

ben: rough hypothesis: kernel cache key is depending on sequence-length bucket + kv cache state, so when KV cache misses we end up using a different codepath and trigger compile.

ryan: yeah that matches. In the trace you can see KV cache miss at ~0.15s then a compile start at ~0.151s. The compile time correlates with sequence_len and prompt prefix size.

jessica: can you paste the small snippet that calculates the cache key?

ryan: snippet: ```python
# simplified key used in runtime
def kernel_key(model_id, seq_len, dtype, optim_flags):
    return f"{model_id}:{seq_len}:{dtype}:{optim_flags}"
```

ben: if seq_len is included verbatim we will compile per-length. Two quick fixes: bucket seq_len (8/16/32/64) or make compile cache insensitive to prefix len for autoreg generation.

maria: bucket idea ok, but we need to measure correctness impact. Some kernels have fusion patterns that are seq-sensitive.

perf-bot: nsys summary: compile_events=13, avg_compile_ms=38.7, compile_cpu=70% of time during spike. Hot kernels: fused_attention, kv_update.

jessica: I'll add a microbench to reproduce locally and test bucketed-key vs agnostic-key. Creating a PR with repro harness.

ryan: repro steps I used: 1) cold clip KV cache, 2) send a short prefix (8 tokens) then a long generation request (64 tokens) forcing fallback kernel, 3) trace with `nsys profile -o out.nsys --trace=nvtx,cuda -- python run_repro.py`.

ben: can we also log kernel_cache hits/misses with sequence-bucket and kv_present flags? small telemetry helps.

maria: agree — add counters: kernel_cache_lookup, kernel_cache_miss, compile_started. Expose via /metrics for a short window.

ryan: filed infra ticket to add ephemeral metrics on canary: INF-3245. I'll drop logs and the nsys tarball there.

jessica: quick note: if we bucket seq_len we should ensure the kernel selector still considers kv cache size so we don't regress memory usage.

ben: next steps: (1) jessica add repro + PR, (2) telemetry + metrics on canary, (3) try bucketed-key patch and run A/B traces, (4) measure perf impact on throughput.

maria: sounds good. tagging @ben to take lead on telemetry. :thumbsup:

ryan: thanks — will keep trace links and raw nsys in INF-3245. If someone can run a quick perfetto flamegraph for the compile hot window that would help prioritize kernel work. :)
